archetype: AZORIUS PILLOW FORT + GROUP HUG + LIGHT TAX, WINNING WITHOUT ATTACKING. Deter the table's combat, hand the whole pod cards, out-use the shared resource through converters only you control, and win from nowhere with the second cast of Approach of the Second Sun. The three legs, verified against the 99: GROUP HUG / table draw runs deep (Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Kami of the Crescent Moon, Dictate of Kruphix, Temple Bell, Mikokoro, Kwain, Loran, The Second Doctor, Horn of Greed, Scrawling Crawler on the gift side; Consecrated Sphinx, Faerie Mastermind, Gleaming Splendor, Smothering Tithe, Prosperity, Skyscribing beside it); PILLOW FORT is Archangel of Tithes, Ghostly Prison, Propaganda, The Second Doctor plus Rhystic Study and Mystic Remora; and TAX is the lightest leg at TWO cards (Rhystic Study, Mystic Remora), which is worth stating plainly rather than calling the deck stax. THE CLOCK IS THE PLAN, NOT A FAILURE OF IT. strategy:multiplayer.pod-management is explicit: 'Manage pace toward the game length your deck wins — engines want the game slow until the pivot window'. strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock's Commander correction says this is the format's default: 'four-player games trend long, so inevitability compounds — engines are the default winning plan and aggro must instead compress the game before the table's late game arrives'. A deck built of Propaganda and Ghostly Prison cannot credibly threaten combat and should not try: strategy:combat-math.racing's correction is that 'you cannot race three life totals'. THE COMMANDER IS THE CONVERTER, NOT THE THREAT. Heliod, the Warped Eclipse reads 'You may cast spells as though they had flash. Spells you cast cost {1} less to cast for each card your opponents have drawn this turn' (oracle text, cards.json), so the discount is largest on an opponent's turn -- exactly where a draw-go fort spends mana, and exactly what makes a {6}{W} sorcery castable while holding a counter. strategy:deckbuilding.archetype-selection's Walser distinction sits precisely: 'built around your commander is not reliant on it. A deck whose only payoff sits in the command zone hands three opponents one target' -- here the PAYOFF is in the 99 and only the ECONOMY is in the command zone. v1.4.0 is three swaps on v1.3.0: Alhammarret's Archive {5} -> Gleaming Splendor {1}{W} (a fuel slot becomes a conversion slot); Lightning Greaves {2} -> Greater Auramancy {1}{W} (mobile protection becomes static, board-wide protection, at the cost of the deck's only Equipment and only haste); one Plains -> one Island. deck-facts (sha f7e21dc6) finds ONE contained combo line -- Approach of the Second Sun + Mystical Tutor, bracket 3, mana_value_needed 15, produces ['Win the game'] -- and two_card_infinites 0.

role_assignment.default_role: THE INEVITABILITY SEAT. strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock defines the resource this deck is actually playing for: 'Inevitability is Duke's name for ownership of the long game: if one player is virtually guaranteed to win a game that goes long enough, that player has it — and knowing whether it's you decides your role.' It then enumerates the sources verbatim -- 'superior late-game card quality, an engine that scales, an unanswerable finisher, or simply more answers than the opponent has threats' -- and this deck is built on THREE of the four. The engine that scales is the table-draw gift plus five converters (goldfish 'Table draw engine online' 0.921 assembled, 0.828 by turn six, mean turn 2.434 -- the earliest and most reliable group in the file). More answers than threats is deck-audit's interaction axis: 14 copies, verdict 'at' against Walser's 12-15, inside a 21-copy interactive suite. And the finisher is unanswerable in the sense that matters for a fort -- Approach of the Second Sun cannot be blocked, raced, removed, taxed or attacked; it can only be COUNTERED, and stack 002 (checker.verdict == 'pass') proves the deck can walk it through a counter window with Swan Song held. SO THE ROLE IS CONTROL, AND UNUSUALLY FOR A CONTROL DECK IT IS THE CORRECT ASSIGNMENT RATHER THAN THE DEFAULT ONE. strategy:whos-the-beatdown's operational test -- 'who has inevitability? — whoever loses the long game must be the beatdown' -- resolves in your favour at any table whose other seats win through combat or accumulation. Apply its table test, 'picture turn 15 with both players on their best draws — whoever likes that picture less should be attacking now': at turn 15 with the fort up you have a full grip, Treasures, three taxers and Approach twice over, and the aggro seats have nothing left. You like that picture. THE ONE TABLE WHERE THE ASSIGNMENT FLIPS is the seat that also owns a late game -- a combo deck, or another engine. strategy:whos-the-beatdown's Commander correction makes that assignable per-seat rather than per-game: 'role is seat-relative — you can be the beatdown against one opponent and the control against another in the same turn cycle; assign per-threat, not per-game'. Against the combo seat you are the beatdown on the Approach clock even while you are the fort to everyone else, and log 002 is that lesson paid for: 'Oliver assembled his one-card Cranko line while the table beat on me.' POSTURE. Pass with mana up, act at instant speed, let the table fight -- which is strategy:multiplayer.pod-management's closing sentence built into a deck: 'Leaving instant-speed mana open forces three players, not one, to respect your possible interaction.' And strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry's rule, 'Your cards should do something to all three seats or win the game; anything else is someone else's job', is satisfied by BOTH halves of this list in the doc's own disjunction: the gift and the fort touch all three seats, and Approach wins the game.
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: WHEN TO STOP HUGGING. The fort does not fail when it is broken; it fails when the table stops believing it. strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection prices that directly -- 'The deflection budget spends down as your engine shows; plan the pivot before it runs out' -- and it also names why a group-hug deck's cover is thinner than it feels: 'combo decks look non-threatening while advancing in secret, which is exactly why experienced tables hit the quiet ramp player — so expect your own "I haven't done anything" to be discounted by anyone tracking mana and draw engines' A player who has been GIVING everyone cards for six turns is the most-tracked seat at an experienced table, not the least. Log 002 records the budget running out in one turn: 'Tithe made me the target immediately and I had no creatures out.' THE WINDOW ITSELF. strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window: 'The window opens when your win attempt either can't be profitably answered — protection up, table tapped out, interaction counted and accounted for — or doesn't need to resolve fully to leave you ahead.' Approach fails the second clause outright (a countered Approach is a card gone, no life, no win check), so the FIRST clause carries the whole decision, and the section's standard is the exact standard the table will apply to you: 'late-game threat assessment collapses to "does this card win the game if it resolves," and that is exactly the standard the table applies to YOUR attempt — assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal, and count the table's open mana before committing.' CONCRETE TRIGGER, four parts. (1) The FIRST Approach has resolved -- you gained 7 and it went seventh from the top; that cast is cheap, unthreatening and should happen as early as you can afford it, because it is the half of the win that nobody reads as a win attempt. (2) Approach is back in hand, by draw depth or by Mystical Tutor / Long-Term Plans. (3) You can pay {6}{W} less that turn's discount with a counter still up -- goldfish mean_available_mana_by_turn crosses seven between turn 7 (6.411) and turn 8 (7.062) with the discount switched OFF, so turn 7-8 is the floor and the discount pulls it earlier. (4) The table's open mana is counted. WHERE TO CAST IT: strategy:tempo.sequencing's Commander correction -- 'prefer committing at the end step before your own turn so the table's chances to respond are spent' -- which for a sorcery needs the flipped Heliod's flash grant or Leyline of Anticipation on the battlefield (candidate line, not fact). THE FAILURE MODE IS WAITING, NOT COMMITTING. strategy:pivot-point: 'hold the protection spell for the turn you commit, not after'. Log 002: the pilot sat on Long-Term Plans overthinking a cost that 'with the treasure and the discount it is two or three, not seven. I waited, got desperate, and the window closed.' strategy:resource-hedging names it -- 'playing *scared* is paying real equity to dodge specific cards' -- and its rule of thumb, 'hedge from ahead, gamble from behind', says that at 0 wins in 2 logged games the correction runs toward taking the window a turn early rather than a turn late.

engines.engine: THE WIN CONDITION, AND IT IS THE RIGHT ONE FOR THIS ARCHETYPE. '{6}{W} Sorcery. If this spell was cast from your hand and you've cast another spell named Approach of the Second Sun this game, you win the game. Otherwise, put Approach of the Second Sun into its owner's library seventh from the top and you gain 7 life' (oracle text, cards.json). It asks for TWO things -- turns and cards -- and asks for nothing else: no board, no combat, no permanents to protect, no opponent cooperation. Those are precisely the two things a fort plus a table-draw engine manufactures. The seven-from-the-top clause is a DRAW-DEPTH problem and this deck is a draw-depth machine; Mystical Tutor shortcuts it entirely, which is what the passing stack proves. The first cast gains 7 life, which is a fort payment in its own right -- strategy:life-as-resource: life's 'points appreciate as they dwindle, so early points are cheap and late points are priceless', and a fort's life is spent late. And it wins WITHOUT ATTACKING, the only kind of win available to a deck that taxes attackers and arms the table.
engines.evidence: oracle text, cards.json; VERIFIED STACK 002 'Approach of the Second Sun, second cast off Mystical Tutor', checker.verdict == 'pass' -- the only rules-verified line in this deck, and the checker's findings confirm the cast-from-hand fact is settled while the spell is on the stack (601.2i) and that the counter window is the stack's own (117.4); deck-facts contained combo line Approach + Mystical Tutor, bracket 3, mana_value_needed 15, produces ['Win the game']; Forge b0f44e4a (v1.2.1, six cards behind the current list): Approach cast 39 times in 120 games, 12 games reached the second cast and ALL TWELVE WON, and 12 of the run's 20 wins read won_by "effect of 'Approach of the Second Sun'"

engines.piece: Propaganda, Ghostly Prison, Archangel of Tithes, The Second Doctor, Rhystic Study, Mystic Remora
engines.engine: THE FORT, and in the doc's accounting it is not defence -- it is card advantage. strategy:card-advantage.virtual's Commander correction is the whole design case, verbatim: 'virtual advantage triples — one tax or pillow-fort effect can blank attack plans from three players at once, the cheapest way to "answer" ~120 life worth of aggression'. Propaganda and Ghostly Prison tax attackers generically; Archangel of Tithes taxes attacking AND blocking and is a 3/4 flier, so it is the one fort piece that is also a body; The Second Doctor buys peace with the gift itself. Rhystic Study and Mystic Remora are the TAX leg and read a CAST, not a draw -- LaPage's taxonomy in strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial places them exactly: 'taxes raise the price of converting resources'. Both can be paid off, which is what makes them political rather than punitive: they are strategy:multiplayer.politics' 'engineered dilemmas' in permanent form.
engines.evidence: oracle text, cards.json; deck-audit interaction-breadth reads 3 of 5 classes; goldfish target 'A taxer down (attackers pay, flying or not)' (Propaganda, Ghostly Prison, Archangel of Tithes) 0.509 assembled / 0.370 by turn six; target 'A body that can block a FLIER' 0.683 / 0.534, whose own label records that 39 of 53 eliminations in the Forge record came from the air. NOTE THE INSTRUMENT: the goldfish has no opponents, so none of these six cards deters, taxes or blanks anything inside it -- their measured contribution there is zero by construction, not by weakness

engines.piece: Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Kami of the Crescent Moon, Dictate of Kruphix, Temple Bell, Mikokoro Center of the Sea, Kwain Itinerant Meddler, Loran of the Third Path, The Second Doctor, Horn of Greed, Scrawling Crawler
engines.engine: THE GIFT -- ignition, and the bargain the whole deck is built on. Eleven permanents that hand cards to players who are not you: eight say 'each player' or 'that player', Kwain says 'each player may draw', Loran alone says 'you and target opponent' (enumerated over cards.json oracle text). The bargain is political before it is mechanical -- strategy:multiplayer.politics: 'Political cards are engineered dilemmas ... they work because opponents facing unknown choices accept bad terms rather than risk falling behind, so offer deals where every possible answer profits you', and 'Position yourself so eliminating you is never anyone's most profitable line until you're winning that turn.' THE SPLIT THAT DECIDES SEQUENCING: Howling Mine, Font, Kami and Dictate fire in each player's DRAW STEP -- on their turn, so they add nothing to Heliod's discount on yours -- while Temple Bell, Mikokoro, Kwain, Loran and The Second Doctor fire ON DEMAND and therefore on your turn, where the discount is spendable. The on-demand half can also be DECLINED, which is the whole answer to a table that is out-using your gift.
engines.evidence: oracle text, cards.json; engine.json ignition stage; goldfish 'Table draw engine online' 0.921 assembled / 0.828 by turn six / mean turn 2.434 -- the earliest and most reliable group in the file, 11 cards, 57% in an opening seven; deck-facts notes: Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Dictate of Kruphix and Ghostly Prison are among the 12 entries card_roles.json has no pattern for -- the gift and the fort are both nearly invisible to the role taxonomy, so every role-derived count on this deck is a floor

engines.piece: Consecrated Sphinx, Faerie Mastermind, Gleaming Splendor, Smothering Tithe, Scrawling Crawler
engines.engine: CONVERSION -- the five cards that make the symmetric gift asymmetric, enumerated over cards.json oracle text as the cards whose trigger is an opponent DRAWING. Only Smothering Tithe can be declined, for {2}; the other four are unconditional. This is where strategy:card-advantage's Commander correction is earned or not: 'engines that out-draw three players are the format's defining advantage'. Note the word is OUT-draw. A symmetric gift alone is not out-drawing anybody; these five are what convert a shared resource into an unshared one, which is why the sequencing rule is converter first, gift second.
engines.evidence: oracle text, cards.json; engine.json conversion stage; deck-audit card-advantage axis 15 copies, verdict 'at' against strategy:deckbuilding.ratios' '10 card draw'; goldfish meta.card_advantage: cards_that_draw 14 against modelled 5, with Consecrated Sphinx, Faerie Mastermind, Gleaming Splendor, Mystic Remora and Rhystic Study all in draw_not_modelled

engines.engine: V1.4.0's structural swap, and a converter HARD-GATED ON IGNITION. 'Whenever an opponent draws their second card each turn, you create a Treasure token. {2}{W}: Two target players each draw a card' (oracle text, cards.json). A natural draw step is ONE card, so with no gift piece on the battlefield the trigger never fires at all -- the card is dead until the engine is already running. Exactly two cards in the 99 carry that trigger condition (Gleaming Splendor and Faerie Mastermind) and exactly three cards make Treasure (An Offer You Can't Refuse, Gleaming Splendor, Smothering Tithe), both enumerated over cards.json oracle text. With a draw-step gift online it has three seats to fire on per turn cycle from a {1}{W} enchantment, and Treasure is the only mana in this deck that BANKS ACROSS TURNS -- which is what turns a {6}{W} sorcery into something a fort can afford while holding a counter. Its own '{2}{W}: Two target players each draw a card' is ignition on an activated ability, and an ability is not a spell, so Heliod's back face never discounts it.
engines.evidence: oracle text, cards.json; engine.json ignition->conversion line via Howling Mine + Gleaming Splendor, verified_by null, 'Claim, not fact'; log 002 in the pilot's own words -- 'with the treasure and the discount it is two or three, not seven'; NOT MEASURED ANYWHERE: goldfish_targets sets model_treasures false and, per engine.json open_questions[4], the harness has no opponents to draw cards even if it were true

engines.engine: THE ECONOMY. 'You may cast spells as though they had flash. Spells you cast cost {1} less to cast for each card your opponents have drawn this turn.' Both halves serve the fort: flash is what lets a draw-go deck spend mana without breaking posture, and the discount is largest on an OPPONENT'S turn, which is when a fort acts. Together they are what makes a {6}{W} sorcery castable in a window where the table's mana is already spent. Heliod is a Legendary Enchantment Creature on both faces (type_line, cards.json) -- which is why Greater Auramancy covers him and why Karametra's Blessing's enchantment-creature clause applies to him. Flip costs {3}{U/P} at sorcery speed on top of {2}{W}{W}; the two Medallions reduce SPELL costs and tap for nothing, so they cannot pay any part of that activation.
engines.evidence: oracle text, cards.json; goldfish commander mean_cast_turn 4.245, cast_by_turn_6_rate 0.886; target 'Heliod plus the mana to flip him' 0.728 / 0.554; target 'Heliod down with an asymmetric card engine' 0.785 / 0.571. THE DISCOUNT IS NOT MODELLED AT ALL -- engine.json states model-coverage gives Heliod no cost channel -- so every mana figure on this deck is a FLOOR

engines.engine: V1.4.0's protection swap, and a TWO-SIDED constraint the frame treats as a real cost. 'Other enchantments you control have shroud' covers TEN of the eleven enchantments in the 99 -- Dictate of Kruphix, Ghostly Prison, Gleaming Splendor, Heliod, Leyline of Anticipation, Mystic Remora, Propaganda, Rhystic Study, Smothering Tithe, Teferi's Ageless Insight, enumerated from type lines, Auramancy excepting itself. For a deck whose fort AND economy are both enchantments that is close to ideal, and it answers log 001 exactly: 'I cast Swords to Plowshares, Alex redirected it onto Heliod. Engine offline from there.' THE COST: shroud stops YOUR targeting too. Karametra's Blessing targets a creature; Guardian of Faith phases out 'other target creatures you control'; neither can be aimed at Heliod while Auramancy is out -- which is the WRATH answer gone, and this deck casts its own wraths (log 002: 'Supreme Verdict after Heliod was already out. I killed my own commander'). Teferi's Protection does not target and is unaffected. THE WAY OUT, enumerated over cards.json: Auramancy does not shroud itself, and four cards can remove it -- Cathar Commando ('{1}, Sacrifice this creature: Destroy target artifact or enchantment', with Flash), Disenchant, Otawara Soaring City's channel, and Loran of the Third Path's ETB. Three are instant-speed, so the Blessing line is recoverable inside one priority window at the price of a second card. CALIBRATION: the self-targeting cost is not new in KIND -- Lightning Greaves also granted shroud ('Equipped creature has haste and shroud', corpus oracle via card-search) -- but Greaves was optional and could simply be left off Heliod, whereas Auramancy is static and board-wide and must be destroyed to switch off.
engines.evidence: oracle text, cards.json; corpus card-search for Lightning Greaves; engine.json protection stage and open_questions[0], settled_by resolve-stack; goldfish target 'Heliod protected, or a flash grant that does not need him' 0.679 assembled / 0.529 by turn six on the REPAIRED declaration (it had been counting Lightning Greaves, a card the merge cut, which deflated it); deck-audit protection axis 5 copies, verdict 'at' against strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density's '5-7 protection slots'

engines.piece: What v1.4.0 REMOVED: Lightning Greaves (the deck's only Equipment and only haste)
engines.engine: PROTECTION IS THINNER IN ONE DIMENSION EVEN AS IT WIDENS IN ANOTHER, and v1.4.0 should not be read as a straight upgrade. Enumerated over cards.json: ZERO cards in the 99 now have 'Equipment' in a type line and ZERO carry the word 'haste' in any face's oracle text. The concrete consequence for THIS archetype: Kwain, Itinerant Meddler and Loran of the Third Path are {T} abilities on non-haste bodies, so each now waits a full turn cycle before it can ignite the engine -- and both belong to the on-demand half of the gift, the half that fires on YOUR turn where the discount lives. strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance's taxonomy prices the trade honestly: Auramancy is 'constant protection (boots-style equipment and enchantments — always on, cheap to re-arm, useless against wraths)'. The doc's own words say it is useless against wraths -- and under Auramancy the deck's two targeted wrath answers are switched off as well until it is destroyed. That is the real cost of the swap, and it is not a footnote.
engines.evidence: cards.json type-line and oracle-text enumeration: 0 Equipment, 0 cards containing 'haste'; corpus card-search: Lightning Greaves 'Equipped creature has haste and shroud. Equip {0}'; goldfish target 'Heliod protected...' 0.679 / 0.529 after the declaration was repaired. CORRECTION CARRIED FORWARD: the old copy's claim that Lightning Greaves was 'the one insurance card Forge ever used' is FALSE -- Karametra's Blessing was cast 9 times in the same 120 games

engines.piece: Counterspell, Swan Song, An Offer You Can't Refuse, Dovin's Veto, Arcane Denial, Archmage's Charm, Force of Negation, Fierce Guardianship
engines.engine: EIGHT true counterspells, enumerated twice and agreeing (deck-facts role 'counterspell' = 8; oracle search for 'counter target' = the same 8). For this archetype they do three jobs at once: they are the fort's answer to what a tax cannot stop, they are the escort for the second Approach, and they are the posture itself. strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite: 'Answers to answers are a separate budget — Commander Deck Maker: 2-4 protection generic, 4-6 combo, 6-8 Voltron; counterspells do both jobs.'
engines.evidence: deck-facts roles histogram counterspell: 8; deck-audit interaction axis 14 copies inside a 21-copy interactive suite, verdict 'at' against 12-15; goldfish 'Free or cheap interaction held' 0.836 assembled / 0.704 by turn six; interaction_in_hand_by_turn 0.929 at t6 against interaction_castable_by_turn 0.627 at t6 -- a thirty-point gap between holding an answer and being able to pay for it

engines.piece: Mystical Tutor, Long-Term Plans, Enlightened Tutor, Drift of Phantasms (transmute)
engines.engine: FOUR tutors, TWO of which cannot find the win condition: Enlightened Tutor fetches an artifact or enchantment and Approach is a sorcery; Drift of Phantasms' transmute finds a mana-value-THREE card and Approach is seven. Only Mystical Tutor and Long-Term Plans reach it. For a deck whose plan is ONE card cast twice, that is the single highest-leverage count in the list. strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors supplies the arithmetic: 'a named card is 7.1% of your opening seven, 10.1% by ten cards seen', and 'A tutor is "essentially an additional copy of any card in our deck" ... k tutors plus the card act like k+1 copies of *every* card' -- so effective copies of the win condition is THREE, not five. The section also names the mitigation this archetype already has: 'Keep rates track enabler-class density, not tutor count' -- and the enabler class here (the gift) is 11 cards deep at 0.921 assembly.
engines.evidence: oracle text, cards.json; engine.json fuel stage; goldfish 'Win condition access' declares exactly three cards (Approach, Mystical Tutor, Long-Term Plans), 0.494 assembled / 0.364 by turn six; bracket_report tutors list is Drift of Phantasms + Long-Term Plans (Mystical and Enlightened are counted as Game Changers instead)

engines.piece: Teferi's Ageless Insight, Braingeyser, Stroke of Genius, Prosperity, Skyscribing, Mathemagics, Dig Through Time, Isochron Scepter
engines.engine: FUEL -- the draw depth that gets back to the seventh-from-the-top Approach, which is the entire cost of the first cast. v1.4.0 made this stage thinner: cutting Alhammarret's Archive and putting nothing back leaves exactly ONE card in the 99 that doubles your own draw, Teferi's Ageless Insight ('draw two cards instead', enumerated over cards.json). That is the clearest structural consequence of the merge -- fuel narrowed so conversion could widen. Note the counting trap strategy:deckbuilding.ratios flags -- 'they are counts of *functions*, not cards, so a card doing two jobs fills two slots' -- Prosperity and Skyscribing are symmetric and so are simultaneously fuel AND ignition, and Mikokoro is simultaneously a land and a gift.
engines.evidence: oracle text, cards.json; engine.json fuel stage; goldfish 'An X-spell finisher drawn' 0.793 assembled / 0.671 by turn six; goldfish model assumption: an {X} draw spell 'is cast AFTER every other loop has spent what it wanted ... and only when X would be at least 2', which makes that channel a floor; engine.json open_questions[2] asks whether the discount lets you choose a larger X and nothing on disk settles it

engines.piece: Psychosis Crawler, Scrawling Crawler, Secure the Wastes, Walking Ballista, Hangarback Walker
engines.engine: THE SECONDARY OUTPUT, and the frame is explicit that it is a BACKUP rather than the plan. Scrawling Crawler drains 1 per opponent draw and doubles as a gift piece; Psychosis Crawler drains 1 per YOUR draw on a body sized to your hand; the other three turn leftover mana into counters or tokens. deck-audit's threat-density axis counts Approach + Psychosis Crawler + Scrawling Crawler as THREE finishers and returns 'at' against Zupke's floor of 3; engine.json's wincon stage counts ONE. Both readings are defensible and the frame reports both: the drains are a real alternate route in a long game and a poor one under a clock. strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density names the choice without calling it wrong: 'Separate ceiling from median: the ceiling build runs one spectacular finisher and loses when it's answered; the median runs three cheap ones and closes from any board.' This deck is deliberately the ceiling build, and the prescription that follows is protection and counter-escort for the one window -- which the deck has, at 8 counters and 5 protection slots.
engines.evidence: oracle text, cards.json; deck-audit threat-density axis value 3, verdict 'at', quote 'Countable floor, Zupke's structure: 3-5 finishers, "at least 3 finishers in your deck"' sourced strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density; engine.json wincon stage single_point_of_failure 'Approach of the Second Sun'; goldfish 'Table draw engine plus a draw-triggered drain, both drawn' 0.321 assembled / 0.189 by turn six -- the weakest group in the file; Forge b0f44e4a (v1.2.1): Psychosis Crawler cast 0 times and discarded 10 (the held-and-never-cast floor condition -- Forge has never tested the card), Scrawling Crawler cast 46 times, and NONE of the 20 wins read won_by a drain

engines.piece: Day of Judgment, Supreme Verdict, Cyclonic Rift
engines.engine: THE RESET BUTTON A FORT NEEDS, and the sequencing trap it creates. A pillow fort loses to a board it cannot tax away; two sweepers and an overloadable bounce are the answer of last resort. strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math's Commander correction is the operating rule: 'assume the wrath — over a four-player game one is near-certain — so deploy in waves, hold a rebuild package, and when possible let another player's board be the reason it gets cast'. For this deck the last clause is strongest: your fort makes attacking unprofitable, so let the boards pile up against SOMEONE ELSE and cast the Verdict when it costs you least. THE TRAP is your own commander: log 002's first recorded error was 'Supreme Verdict after Heliod was already out. I killed my own commander' -- and under Greater Auramancy the repair is harder, since Karametra's Blessing cannot target him until Auramancy is gone.
engines.evidence: oracle text, cards.json; deck-audit sweepers axis value 2, verdict 'under', gap 3 -- against a target whose own quote reads 'wipes "one or two max" (Zupke caps at 3)', sourced strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite. The axis and the section it cites disagree; the frame reports both and takes no side

engines.piece: 33 land copies in 18 entries, seven rocks, Pearl and Sapphire Medallion
engines.engine: MANA -- what pays {6}{W} twice while a counter stays up, and it is short of the yardstick. deck-facts: 33 land copies, 18 entries, 7 entering tapped, land sources 23 U / 20 W against a Karsten source target of 36 apiece. v1.4.0's third swap lives here: one Plains -> one Island, moving a basic from the lighter-pip colour to the heavier one (pips 0.611 U / 0.389 W). It does not close a twelve-source gap and nothing claims it does. TREASURE IS THE REAL ANSWER for this archetype, not lands: it banks across turns, which is what a fort needs to cast a seven-drop in a window it chose rather than a turn it reached -- and v1.4.0 doubled the count of permanents that make it from one to two.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Breaking your own Greater Auramancy in one priority window to make Karametra's Blessing legal under a wrath
cards: Heliod, the Radiant Dawn // Heliod, the Warped Eclipse
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: The shroud question itself is ALREADY FILED as engine.json open_questions[0] (settled_by resolve-stack), so this entry queues the LINE that follows from it rather than re-asking it. Auramancy says 'Other enchantments you control have shroud' and excepts itself; four cards in the 99 can remove it (enumerated over cards.json oracle text): Cathar Commando ('{1}, Sacrifice this creature: Destroy target artifact or enchantment', Flash), Disenchant, Otawara Soaring City's channel, and Loran of the Third Path's ETB -- three of them instant-speed. THE CLAIMED SEQUENCE: a wrath is on the stack; you destroy your own Auramancy in response; it resolves; with priority back and the wrath still on the stack, Karametra's Blessing becomes a legal target on Heliod and grants indestructible ('If it's an enchanted creature or enchantment creature, it also gains hexproof and indestructible until end of turn' -- Heliod's type line is Legendary Enchantment Creature on both faces). If it holds, the fort's commander survives a wrath at the price of one extra card and the 0.679 protection assembly figure is honest. If the timing does not work as claimed, two of five protection slots are mutually exclusive with the third whenever it is on the battlefield, and the figure overstates real coverage.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Gleaming Splendor's trigger count per turn cycle, and whether its own activated ability feeds it
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: The entire case for v1.4.0's first swap is that 'Whenever an opponent draws their second card each turn' fires on THREE seats every turn the gift runs, with Howling Mine ('at the beginning of each player's draw step, that player draws an additional card') supplying the second card on each opponent's own turn. Nothing on disk states the per-opponent-per-turn count. Separately, if Gleaming Splendor's own '{2}{W}: Two target players each draw a card', aimed at an opponent who has already drawn once this turn, counts as their second, the card is an ignition piece and a converter in one -- which changes both how it is played and how the fort finances itself. No goldfish target measures it (model_treasures is false and the harness has no opponents to draw cards), and no Forge run has ever contained the card. Recorded as engine.json open_questions[1].

candidate_missing_lines.title: The second Approach at an opponent's end step under Heliod's flash grant, with Fierce Guardianship live
cards: Heliod, the Radiant Dawn // Heliod, the Warped Eclipse
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: This is the highest-leverage unresolved question on the deck, because it is the one that widens the pivot window a fort has waited ten turns to take. strategy:tempo.sequencing's Commander correction says where to commit -- 'prefer committing at the end step before your own turn so the table's chances to respond are spent' -- and for a sorcery that requires the back face's 'You may cast spells as though they had flash' or Leyline of Anticipation. Stack 002 (pass) resolves only the sorcery-speed cast on your own turn, so the end-step window is unproven. Whether Fierce Guardianship's free alternative cost is live in that window turns on Heliod being on the battlefield as your commander, which the flash grant already presupposes. In Forge b0f44e4a, 12 of 120 games reached a second Approach and all twelve won. Recorded as engine.json open_questions[3].

candidate_missing_lines.title: How large the discount actually gets on an opponent's turn, and whether it can raise X
cards: Heliod, the Radiant Dawn // Heliod, the Warped Eclipse
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: The back face counts 'each card your opponents have drawn this turn'. On an opponent's turn their draw step is one, Howling Mine a second, Font of Mythos two more, a land drop under Horn of Greed another -- so the reduction on a spell cast in that window is plausibly {3} to {5}, which is the difference between Approach costing {6}{W} and costing {1}{W}. The pilot already wrote the line by hand in log 002: 'with the treasure and the discount it is two or three, not seven.' Separately, whether the reduction lets you choose a larger X on Braingeyser, Stroke of Genius, Prosperity, Skyscribing or Mathemagics -- and whether X is chosen before or after the reduction -- is what the 0.793-assembly 'X-spell finisher' group rests on. Nothing in stacks/ resolves a single discounted cast and the goldfish has no channel for the discount at all. Recorded as engine.json open_questions[2].

candidate_missing_lines.title: Isochron Scepter imprinting Mystical Tutor as a repeatable route back to Approach
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Stack 002 verifies Mystical Tutor putting Approach on top for the second cast. A Scepter copy at each opponent's end step would repeat that for {2} without spending a card, widening the three-card 'Win condition access' group (0.494 assembled) into something repeatable -- and for a deck whose plan is one card cast twice, access is the binding constraint, not conversion. Unsettled: whether a Scepter-created copy cast without paying its mana cost behaves as stack 002's cast does, what Mystical Tutor's shuffle does to an Approach already seventh from the top, and whether the Scepter's {2} activation is reduced by Heliod (it is an ability, not a spell, so it should not be -- worth proving rather than assuming).

candidate_missing_lines.title: Psychosis Crawler as the fort's second win route in a game that goes past turn fifteen
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: The only line in the 99 that converts the engine into damage without Approach: 'Whenever you draw a card, each opponent loses 1 life', on a body whose power equals your hand size. Under Teferi's Ageless Insight ('draw two cards instead') and Consecrated Sphinx it is a multi-point drain per turn cycle against all three seats, which is exactly the shape strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry endorses -- 'each-opponent drains ... are the payoffs that actually scale'. It has never been priced in either instrument: goldfish's combat model gives kill_by_turn_8 0.009 with drains counted and no blockers, and Forge shows the card cast ZERO times in 120 games while discarded ten, the held-and-never-cast floor condition. Until a scenario or a run prices it, the claim that this deck has a second route is unsupported in both directions -- which matters because the doc's ceiling-build warning ('loses when it's answered') applies only if there is genuinely nothing behind Approach.

matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: THE MATCHUP WHERE INEVITABILITY IS ACTUALLY CONTESTED, and the only one where this deck should consider itself the beatdown. strategy:whos-the-beatdown: 'In every matchup one deck is the beatdown (racing to end the game) and one is the control (aiming for the long game) — and the roles are set by matchup and game state, not your deck's label.' Against a seat that also owns a late game, the tie-break is whose finisher is cheaper and harder to stop; Approach costs {6}{W} twice, so you should be racing to it rather than accumulating past it. Their sweepers cost you very little -- a fort is mostly enchantments and 16 creature copies that are converters rather than a board -- so a wrath is nearly a blank against you and a two-for-four against the aggro seats, which is a gift to your plan. Bank counters for the two Approach casts rather than trading them for value: strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy's bar is 'ends the game or ends my deck's function,' not 'looks scary'. Your OWN sweepers are the trap -- wipe FIRST, then resolve Heliod (log 002), and remember that under Greater Auramancy Karametra's Blessing cannot save him from your own Verdict until Auramancy is destroyed.
matchup_frames.vs_stax: THE WORST MATCHUP, BECAUSE A TAX BEATS A FORT ON THE SAME AXIS THE FORT USES. strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial: 'Decks built on many cheap spells per turn are hit hardest: taxes attack the velocity math directly, so recount your hand under the tax — a two-spell turn becoming a one-spell turn halves the engine.' This deck's modal mana value is 2 with 23 two-drops and 18 three-drops (deck-facts curve), it is already twelve sources short of the Karsten yardstick, and it misses land drops at 0.254. Worse, a fort's whole proposition -- 'attacking me is unprofitable, so go elsewhere' -- is irrelevant to a deck that was never going to attack you. The section forces the role: 'you rarely own the long game under an assembling lock, so you are the beatdown, racing the lock's completion'. Name the outs early per its own instruction -- 'the removal or velocity that breaks the piece that beats *you*, not the scariest piece' -- and here they are four: Disenchant, Cathar Commando, Loran's ETB and Otawara's channel, all cheap enough to cast under a tax. Note deck-audit reads interaction-breadth UNDER at 3 of 5 classes with graveyard and land uncovered, and that counterspells are near-worthless here: 'a counter answers a lock piece only on the way in' (strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite). Johnson's frame, quoted in the same section, is the whole plan: 'stax wins by breaking parity; break it back, or win before it breaks.'
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: THE MATCHUP THE DECK IS BUILT TO WIN, AND THE ONE NO INSTRUMENT ON DISK CAN SEE. strategy:card-advantage.virtual's Commander correction is the thesis verbatim: 'virtual advantage triples — one tax or pillow-fort effect can blank attack plans from three players at once, the cheapest way to "answer" ~120 life worth of aggression'. Propaganda, Ghostly Prison and Archangel of Tithes do not kill attackers, they make attacking YOU the worst available line, and strategy:combat-math.racing's correction explains why that is enough: 'you cannot race three life totals -- races there are two-player subgames run while the rest of the table develops'. Your job is to make sure you are not in anybody's subgame. Two honest weaknesses: the layer is thin (goldfish 'A taxer down' 0.509 assembled, 0.370 by turn six -- the second-weakest group in the file), and the Forge record says 39 of 53 eliminations came from the AIR, against which the fort is generic but the blockers are not (goldfish 'A body that can block a FLIER' 0.683 / 0.534). Deploy the taxers BEFORE the converters, not after -- log 002: 'Tithe made me the target immediately and I had no creatures out. The lesson is to have a shell or blockers around Tithe, or defer deploying it until I do.'
matchup_frames.vs_combo: THE MATCHUP THAT ENDS BEFORE THE FORT'S PLAN DOES, AND THE ONE THE LOG ALREADY LOST. A fort deters combat and a combo deck does not attack; a gift accelerates everyone equally and a combo deck converts cards into a win faster than you do. Log 002: 'Oliver assembled his one-card Cranko line while the table beat on me.' Eight counterspells are genuinely the right tool -- strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite: 'counterspells do both jobs' -- and interaction_in_hand_by_turn is 0.929 at turn six, but interaction_castable_by_turn at the same turn is 0.627, a thirty-point gap between holding an answer and being able to pay for it. The pilot named the archetype's own contribution in log 001: 'making everyone draw also hands everyone answers to my counters. I am symmetrically fuelling the table's ability to fight me.' THE RULE THAT REVERSES HERE: strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy's countervailing clause -- 'held answers rot — against combo, or lethal already on board, the last profitable moment is now.' Against a known combo seat, deploy the draw-step gifts LATE or not at all, prefer the on-demand half (Temple Bell, Mikokoro, Kwain, Loran, The Second Doctor) which you can decline to activate, and treat strategy:resource-hedging.playing-to-outs as the frame -- 'don't play around something you can't beat anyway'.
matchup_frames.vs_another_engine_or_the_mirror: A seat that also converts cards into advantage turns your gift into THEIR fuel at no cost to them. strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry's closing rule is the test -- 'Your cards should do something to all three seats or win the game; anything else is someone else's job' -- and the gift does something to all three seats in the WRONG direction until a converter is down. The sequencing rule that follows: never deploy a draw-step gift (Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Kami of the Crescent Moon, Dictate of Kruphix) before a converter is on the battlefield, and prefer the on-demand gifts, which you control the frequency of. strategy:card-advantage's Commander correction is the standard to hold yourself to: 'engines that out-draw three players are the format's defining advantage' -- OUT-draw, not co-draw. The doc has no section on the group-hug bargain itself, which is the largest gap this frame found.
matchup_frames.political_frame: THE DECK'S FOURTH RESOURCE, AND FOR THIS ARCHETYPE IT IS NOT OPTIONAL. strategy:multiplayer.politics: 'Politics is the fourth resource pillar of multiplayer: attention, favors, and perceived threat are spendable currencies', and 'Political cards are engineered dilemmas ... offer deals where every possible answer profits you.' Howling Mine and Temple Bell ARE that card type, and The Second Doctor buys peace outright. The positioning rule is the fort's thesis in the doc's own words: 'Position yourself so eliminating you is never anyone's most profitable line until you're winning that turn.' THE WARNING THAT APPLIES SPECIFICALLY TO A GENEROUS DECK, from strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection: 'combo decks look non-threatening while advancing in secret, which is exactly why experienced tables hit the quiet ramp player — so expect your own "I haven't done anything" to be discounted by anyone tracking mana and draw engines' A group-hug seat is the most-watched player at a good table, not the least, and 'Know your deck's tells — the cards everyone fears — and time them for the turn they win, not the turn they impress' applies to Smothering Tithe and Rhystic Study above all. Also keep the craft rule: 'never lie outright about game state (credibility is a multi-game resource)' -- this is a deck the same pod will see many times, and its whole economy is other people's trust.

distribution_notes: START WITH THE INSTRUMENT, BECAUSE IT CANNOT SEE THIS ARCHETYPE. The goldfish's own stated assumption is 'Simulates resource development, not full games (no interaction, no removal)', and engine.json open_questions[4] states the consequence flatly: 'The goldfish has no opponents.' For a pillow fort plus group hug that is not a minor gap, it is most of the deck. Propaganda, Ghostly Prison and Archangel of Tithes deter nobody inside it; Rhystic Study and Mystic Remora tax nothing; Smothering Tithe and Gleaming Splendor make no Treasure because nobody draws; the political half does not exist at all. So kill_by_turn_8 0.009, no_kill_by_max_turn_rate 0.865 and median_kill_turn 10 are figures about a deck stripped of its function, and they are ALSO exactly what a deck that taxes attackers and refuses to race is supposed to produce on a combat-only kill metric. Neither reading makes them evidence of a defect. What the goldfish DOES measure honestly on this list is resource development, and there it is good: the gift assembles at 0.921 with mean turn 2.434, interaction is held 0.836 of the time, and extra cards drawn reaches 3.601 by turn ten -- and even that is a floor, because Heliod's discount has no channel (model-coverage gives the commander no cost channel at all) and nine draw sources sit in meta.card_advantage.draw_not_modelled (cards_that_draw 14 against modelled 5). THE CURVE FITS THE PLAN. deck-facts: modal mana value 2, with 11 one-drops, 23 two-drops, 18 three-drops, 9 four-drops and a single card each at 5, 6, 7 and 8. strategy:deckbuilding.curve's reference 'puts the modal mana value at 2, with 15.7 two-drops and 15.4 three-drops in the average deck and only ~1.5 cards at mana value 8+' -- this list is at the mode and above the reference on both the two- and three-drop counts, which is what a deck that wants to hold up two spells a turn should look like. The one seven-drop is the win condition and the one eight is a mana sink. ROLE BALANCE, READ AS A FORT. deck-facts roles: 8 counterspell, 10 draw:engine, 5 draw:wheel, 3 draw:burst, 8 ramp:rock, 3 ramp:treasure, 3 ramp:cost-reduction, 4 removal:spot, 2 removal:sweeper, 5 protection:self, 1 protection:granted, 16 threat:body, 1 wincon:alt, 2 wincon:drain. Coverage is 0.859 and TWELVE cards have no role at all -- Braingeyser, Dictate of Kruphix, Dig Through Time, Font of Mythos, Ghostly Prison, Howling Mine, Leyline of Anticipation, Mathemagics, Propaganda, Reliquary Tower, Skycloud Expanse, Stroke of Genius. Note WHICH cards those are: the gift and the fort. The taxonomy has no pattern for either, so every role-derived count on this deck understates the two things it is actually built on, and deck-facts says so in its own notes: 'Absence of a role is not absence of the function.' AGAINST THE TEMPLATES. strategy:deckbuilding.ratios' Command Zone default is '36–38 lands, 10–12 ramp, 10 card draw, 10–12 targeted removal, 3–4 board wipes' -- this deck is 33 lands (under), 14 ramp copies (over), 15 card-advantage copies (at), 14 interaction copies (at) and 2 wipes. The section's own caveat is the one to apply: 'they are counts of *functions*, not cards, so a card doing two jobs fills two slots', and this list is full of double-counters -- Scrawling Crawler is gift and drain, Mikokoro is land and gift, Loran is gift and artifact/enchantment removal, Prosperity and Skyscribing are fuel and gift, Archangel of Tithes is fort and flier. Hinds' verdict quoted in the same section applies: the template is '"too 'one size fits all'"'. MANA IS THE REAL SHORTFALL. 23 U and 20 W land sources against a Karsten target of 36 apiece, 7 of 18 land entries entering tapped, land_drop_hit_rate falling 0.875 at turn three to 0.536 at turn six. strategy:deckbuilding.mana-base.color-sources is the axis deck-audit reads UNDER on, and the v1.4.0 Plains->Island swap moves one source toward the heavier pip colour without closing the gap. For this archetype the mitigation is Treasure rather than land count, because Treasure banks across turns and a fort casts on the turn it chooses.
overall_assessment: THE WORLD-VIEW: this deck plays the game the strategy doc says Commander defaults to, and it plays it from the one seat that does not need to attack. strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock's Commander correction is the thesis in the literature's own words -- 'four-player games trend long, so inevitability compounds — engines are the default winning plan and aggro must instead compress the game before the table's late game arrives' -- and strategy:multiplayer.pod-management supplies the operating instruction: 'Manage pace toward the game length your deck wins — engines want the game slow until the pivot window.' The three legs do three separable jobs and the doc has a section for each: the FORT is virtual card advantage ('one tax or pillow-fort effect can blank attack plans from three players at once, the cheapest way to "answer" ~120 life worth of aggression' -- strategy:card-advantage.virtual); the GIFT is politics in permanent form ('Political cards are engineered dilemmas' -- strategy:multiplayer.politics) and buys the positioning rule 'eliminating you is never anyone's most profitable line until you're winning that turn'; and the CONVERTERS are what make a shared resource unshared, which is the only way to satisfy strategy:card-advantage's standard, 'engines that out-draw three players are the format's defining advantage' -- out-draw, not co-draw. APPROACH OF THE SECOND SUN IS NOT A THIN WIN CONDITION; IT IS THE CORRECT ONE. It asks for turns and cards and nothing else -- no board, no combat, no cooperation -- which are precisely the two goods a fort and a table-draw engine manufacture. It cannot be blocked, raced, removed or taxed; it can only be countered, and it is the one line in this deck that is RULES-VERIFIED (stack 002, checker.verdict == 'pass', the second cast walking through a counter window with Swan Song held). The first cast gains 7 life, which is itself a fort payment at the point where strategy:life-as-resource says life is dearest ('points appreciate as they dwindle'). And it wins without attacking, which is the only kind of win a deck full of Propaganda and Ghostly Prison can credibly reach. SO THE REAL QUESTION IS NOT 'WHY DOESN'T IT CLOSE' BUT 'WHEN DOES THE FORT STOP HOLDING', and the doc answers that in two places and from two directions. From the political side, strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection: 'The deflection budget spends down as your engine shows; plan the pivot before it runs out' -- and its warning lands hardest on exactly this archetype, because 'experienced tables hit the quiet ramp player', and a seat that has been giving everyone cards for six turns is the most-tracked player at the table, not the least. From the resource side, strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial quotes McGuinness on the same structural problem from the stax seat -- a deck built on parity 'must still turn "how do I not lose" into winning, and that conversion is slow' -- and Johnson's frame, 'stax wins by breaking parity; break it back, or win before it breaks'. Approach IS the parity break, and the whole skill of the deck is choosing its turn. WHAT THE EVIDENCE ACTUALLY SUPPORTS, kept honest: the deck is 0-2 on paper across two logged games and both losses are legible failures of TIMING and SEQUENCING rather than of archetype -- log 001 lost Heliod to a redirected Swords with no protection in the list (which v1.4.0's Greater Auramancy directly answers), and log 002 records three sequencing errors in the pilot's own hand, the central one being 'I sat on Long-Term Plans ... I waited, got desperate, and the window closed.' The Forge record is SIX CARDS BEHIND the current list and describes a different deck; read every rate from it as history. And the Auramancy constraint is real and two-sided: it shrouds ten enchantments including the commander, and it switches off the deck's own Karametra's Blessing and Guardian of Faith until one of four cards destroys it. THE ONE PLACE THE DOC ASKS A HARD QUESTION OF THIS BUILD is strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density: 'Separate ceiling from median: the ceiling build runs one spectacular finisher and loses when it's answered; the median runs three cheap ones and closes from any board.' This is the ceiling build by design, and the prescription that follows from that choice is more escort, not more finishers -- the eight counterspells and five protection slots exist to buy one window, and the tutor count is the number that binds, since two of four tutors cannot find a seven-mana sorcery. The section's closing instruction is the deck's own to-do list: 'Know your number ... then count how many of the 99 produce it.' The number here is two casts, and the cards that produce it are three.
disagreements: GAME CHANGER COUNT. The spawning brief says 'on 10 Game Changers'; bracket_report.json and deck-audit's power axis both enumerate EIGHT (Consecrated Sphinx, Cyclonic Rift, Enlightened Tutor, Fierce Guardianship, Mystical Tutor, Rhystic Study, Smothering Tithe, Teferi's Protection). Both agree the floor is 4 (Optimized) and within_target is true. The frame uses eight and flags the discrepancy rather than picking; bracket_report.json carries no decklist_sha256, so its freshness against f7e21dc6 cannot be checked from the file itself.

FINISHER COUNT. deck-audit's threat-density axis counts 3 (Approach, Psychosis Crawler, Scrawling Crawler) and returns 'at' against Zupke's floor; engine.json's wincon stage counts 1, with single_point_of_failure set. Both are defensible -- the drains are a real route in a very long game and a poor one under a clock -- and no artifact prices the drain. Reported, not resolved.

SWEEPER BAND. deck-audit reads sweepers UNDER at 2 with gap 3, against a target whose own quoted text (from strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite) reads 'wipes "one or two max" (Zupke caps at 3)'. The axis's band and the section it cites disagree. The frame reports both.

FORGE PROVENANCE. Every Forge figure available on this deck comes from run b0f44e4a at seat sha 214af308 (v1.2.1), which is SIX cards behind f7e21dc6 and contains none of v1.4.0's cards. Its 20-in-99 win rate describes a different deck and is cited here only for card-level behaviour (casts, discards, won_by attribution), never as a rate for the current list.

GOLDFISH APPLICABILITY. The goldfish is the only instrument with a current-sha reading, and by its own assumptions it has no opponents -- so for a fort plus group-hug deck it cannot measure deterrence, taxation, opponent-draw Treasure, or politics. Its combat figures are not a verdict on this archetype in either direction.

TWO CORRECTIONS CARRIED FROM THE PROSE, so they are not re-inherited: the claim that Lightning Greaves was 'the one insurance card Forge ever used' is false (Karametra's Blessing was cast 9 times in the same 120 games); and the giada comparison figure is 31 of 32 creatures flying, not 30 of 32 (only Starnheim Aspirant lacks it).
gaps: NO SECTION ON THE GROUP-HUG BARGAIN. This is the largest gap the frame found and it sits under the deck's central card type. Queries 'symmetrical effects that help opponents equally' and 'group hug symmetrical effects who benefits' peak at strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry (0.415) and strategy:card-advantage.virtual (0.234) -- both about ASYMMETRIC effects, which is the opposite question. WANTED: who a symmetric draw effect actually favours in a four-player pod; the conversion ratio at which giving three opponents a card each is net-positive; why the on-demand gift (which you can decline) is a different card from the draw-step gift (which you cannot); and the failure mode the pilot recorded himself in log 001 -- 'making everyone draw also hands everyone answers to my counters. I am symmetrically fuelling the table's ability to fight me.' The doc's nearest usable line is strategy:card-advantage's 'engines that out-draw three players are the format's defining advantage', whose operative word is OUT-draw, and it does not address co-drawing at all.

NO SECTION ON PILOTING A PILLOW FORT. The doc knows the fort exists only as one clause inside strategy:card-advantage.virtual's Commander correction; the query 'pillow fort tax attackers Propaganda Ghostly Prison deterrence' finds nothing above ~0.28. WANTED: how many taxers make a deterrent rather than a speed bump; {2}-per-attacker against a token swarm versus a Voltron commander versus a flier; which routes ignore the fort entirely (fliers, trample, direct damage, mill, alt-win); when a fort should spend its deterrence rather than keep it; and the conversion clock -- how long a fort can hold before the table out-scales it. strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial contains the only usable frame (McGuinness's 'stax must still turn "how do I not lose" into winning, and that conversion is slow'; Johnson's 'stax wins by breaking parity') and it is written from the seat PLAYING AGAINST denial, not from the seat running it.

NO SECTION ON ALTERNATE WIN CONDITIONS AS A CLASS. A 'you win the game' card is not a threat: it cannot be blocked, raced or removed, and the entire skill is one stack window. strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window is closest and is written for board-based kills -- its instruction 'Prefer win attempts that leave a rebuilt position if they fail' is one Approach cannot follow. WANTED: the two-cast / delayed-payoff structure (Approach, Thassa's Oracle, Test of Endurance, Felidar Sovereign) as a class; how many tutors and protection slots one is worth; whether an alt-win counts as a finisher for threat-density purposes; and how to time it across three responders who all know what it does.

NO SECTION ON COST REDUCTION AS A RESOURCE. This deck's economy is a conditional per-spell discount, and the doc has no home for it. WANTED: how to value a conditional discount against a mana rock; why a discount favours cheap generic costs over coloured pips; the difference between reducing a SPELL and paying an ABILITY (which is why the two Medallions cannot help flip Heliod and why Gleaming Splendor's own activation is never discounted); and whether a reduction interacts with X.

NO SECTION ON THE DRAW-GO POSTURE IN A FOUR-PLAYER GAME. The measured gap on this deck is interaction held 0.929 at turn six against interaction castable 0.627 -- thirty points between having the answer and affording it. strategy:multiplayer.pod-management has one sentence on open mana and strategy:tempo one marker on unspent mana. WANTED: how much mana to leave up across a four-player turn cycle, how to price three opponents' turns against your own, and when a fort should break posture to develop.

NO SECTION ON MEASURING A DETERRENCE OR POLITICAL DECK. Not a strategy gap so much as one the frame kept running into: every instrument this project has (goldfish with no opponents, Forge with an AI that does not negotiate) is structurally blind to deterrence and politics. If the doc had a section on what a fort's success LOOKS like -- turns survived, attacks redirected, seats that never pointed at you -- the bench would have something to measure against instead of a kill-turn histogram.

NO SECTION ON REPEATABLE-EFFECT ARTIFACTS (Isochron Scepter and its class). The query 'Isochron Scepter imprint repeatable counterspell value' returns nothing above ~0.15. WANTED: what a repeatable {2} counter or tutor is worth per turn cycle against three responders, which imprints are live, and the tell it hands the table.
